questions.topic: Recombination frequency from a test cross
questions.md:
A scientist is studying two genes, A and B, in a plant species. Gene A controls flower color (red or white) and gene B controls leaf shape (rounded or jagged). The dominant allele A gives red and the recessive a gives white; the dominant allele B gives rounded and the recessive b gives jagged. To study the inheritance, the scientist performs a dihybrid test cross between a plant heterozygous for both traits (AaBb) and a plant homozygous recessive for both (aabb). The offspring are:

- Red flowers, rounded leaves: 40
- Red flowers, jagged leaves: 10
- White flowers, rounded leaves: 12
- White flowers, jagged leaves: 38

i) Exhibit the cross in the form of a Punnett square.

ii) Identify the parental and recombinant phenotypes.

iii) Calculate the recombination frequency for these genes.

iv) Based on your calculations, determine whether these genes are likely linked or assort independently.
